subject.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries

question: Does the linked PR preserve OpenClaw’s intended authorization boundary when protected tool schemas remain prompt-visible but executable authority comes only from an authoritative current-turn policy snapshot?
rationale: Source and tests can establish mechanics, but accepting the separation between model-visible capability and executable owner or trusted-internal authority is a security-boundary decision owned by the repository.

options.title: Approve the separated boundary
options.body: Accept stable prompt-visible schemas with deterministic pre-hook and pre-side-effect denial or grant from the current-turn policy snapshot.

options.title: Request narrower visibility
options.body: Require the PR to reduce which protected schemas remain visible or redesign trusted-internal grants before merge, accepting possible cache-shape tradeoffs.

recommendation.title: Approve the separated boundary
recommendation.body: Accept stable prompt-visible schemas with deterministic pre-hook and pre-side-effect denial or grant from the current-turn policy snapshot.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns the relevant security-sensitive agent and gateway surfaces to this team, and the remaining question specifically concerns authorization boundaries.
